in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: female ICR mice, 8 weeks old, bred at the Department of Laboratory Animal Science of Fudan University
in_vivo_species.quote: 5 mg/kg of a peptide were intraperitoneally (i.p.) injected into four female ICR mice (8 weeks).
in_vivo_species.section: METHODS (4.6 Ex Vivo Anti-HIV-1 Activity and Serum Half-Life of Peptides)

ex_vivo_detail: Serum was collected from peptide-treated female ICR mice before (0 h) and after i.p. injection (0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6 h for HP23-E6-IDL and YIK; 1, 3, 7, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19 h for YIK-C16) and each serum sample was serially diluted and tested for inhibition of HIV-1IIIB infection of MT-2 cells. The highest serum dilution-fold causing 50% inhibition was used as the ex vivo activity readout and to back-calculate the active peptide concentration.
in_vitro_detail: HIV-1 infection inhibition assays (HIV-1IIIB in MT-2 cells, HIV-1Bal in CEMx174 5.25 M7 cells, plus T20-, T2635- and HP23-resistant strains) read out by p24 antigen ELISA; cell-wash and virus-wash binding assays; dye-transfer H9/IIIB-MT-2 cell-cell fusion assay; 6-HB formation inhibition ELISA with N46/C34 and mAb NC-1; CD spectroscopy in PBS; CCK8 cytotoxicity in MT-2 and M7 cells.

concentration_time_figure.locator: Figure 4b (estimated serum concentration vs time); Figure 4a (ex vivo serum anti-HIV-1 activity vs time)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Anti-HIV-1IIIB activity of the serum samples collected from mice at different time points after i.p. administration of HP23-E6-IDL, YIK, and YIK-C16. (b) Concentration of the active peptides in the serum samples was estimated.
concentration_time_figure.note: Figure 4b plots the estimated active-peptide serum concentration against time; the concentrations were not measured directly but back-calculated from the ex vivo serum IC50 relative to the in vitro IC50. Figure 4a plots serum antiviral activity (fold of IC50) against time.

bioanalytical_method: Indirect bioassay rather than a chemical assay: serum dilutions were tested for inhibition of HIV-1IIIB infection of MT-2 cells with p24 antigen ELISA readout, and the active-peptide concentration was back-calculated from the serum IC50 relative to the in vitro IC50; PK parameters fitted with MODFIT software.
bioanalytical_quote: The concentration of an active peptide in serum of a mouse treated with this peptide was estimated based on the IC50 value of the peptide in the mouse serum for inhibiting HIV-1 infection
bioanalytical_section: METHODS (4.6 Ex Vivo Anti-HIV-1 Activity and Serum Half-Life of Peptides)
notes: No mass-spectrometric or immunoassay measurement of peptide concentration was performed; all PK values derive from a bioactivity-based estimate, which the authors justify by citing Chong et al. Group size is stated three different ways in the body: 'Twelve mice ... into three groups' (Results 2.4), 'four female ICR mice (8 weeks)' per peptide (Methods 4.6) and 'n = 3' (Table 2). Peptide amino-acid sequences appear only in Figure 1a, which is not rendered in the text file, so all sequences are recorded as not reported. Full Table 2 parameters for YIK-C16: Tmax 4.0 ± 1.7 h, Cmax 2.2 ± 0.1 μg/mL, t½ 5.9 ± 3.2 h, AUC0-15h 14.9 ± 3.8 h*μg/mL, AUCINF_obs 15.0 ± 3.7 h*μg/mL, Vz 2738.8 ± 740.7 mL/kg, Cl 346.4 ± 76.1 mL/h/kg, MRTlast 9.5 ± 5.1 h. No PK table is given for YIK or HP23-E6-IDL beyond their half-lives. Animal ethics approval 20160927-2 (Fudan University).
